the reconstruction of the sedimentological history of the Bryant and Eastern Canyan area, during the last ∼ 135 kyr, based on the analysis of 48 long piston cores from the area, and the interpretation of their depositional environments and processes.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Mississippi River discharge was a dominant factor in controlling the depositional processes on the continental slope and the abyssal plain of northwest Gulf of Mexico since the last glacial period.
the evolution and sedimentation in the canyons were strongly controlled by sea level, and the Mississippi River discharge was the major source of sediments for the continental slope.
the Mississippi River has been the main source of sediment for the continental slope and the abyssal plain of northwest Gulf of Mexico since at least MIS 6.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Mississippi River is the main source of sediment to the northwest Gulf of Mexican slope and abyssal plains during glacial periods, whereas during interglacial periods, the Mississippi River sediments remain confined to the continental shelf.
the Mississippi River has played an important role in the development of the Bryant Canyon area during the last glaciation.
the Mississippi River discharge is a major factor controlling the sedimentation in the Gulf of Mexico, but the sedimentary response to this factor is strongly modulated by the sea level.
The main takeaway from our work is that

sedimentation on the upper and middle slope of the northwest continental margin of the Gulf of Mexico is mainly related to river-sourced sedi-ments and the sedimentation on the lower slope and abyssal plains is related to the entrainment of wash-load and tails from the Mississippi Fan.
the evolution of the canyonal system is controlled by the interplay between sea-level changes, river discharges and salt tectonics.
the evolution of the canyonal systems of the northwest Gulf is controlled by a complex interaction between glacio-eustatic sea-level changes, river discharges and halokinetic activity.
